1: # QA & release workflows: delegate the specific objective
2: 
3: Always inspect installed TEA skills and their own inputs/outputs. TEA is an
4: optional BMAD module. QA does not mean "run everything" and code review is not
5: an interchangeable substitute for executable tests.
6: 
7: | Exact request | Native owner if installed | Actual deliverable |
8: |---|---|---|
9: | "Review code/PR/diff" | `bmad-code-review` | findings, triage and optional patches if authorized |
10: | "Generate E2E tests" | `bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests` | executable tests, actual run results |
11: | "Plan QA / risk matrix" | `bmad-testarch-test-design` | scenario/risk plan |
12: | "Tests before dev / ATDD" | `bmad-testarch-atdd` | failing acceptance scaffolds (red expected) |
13: | "Improve automated coverage" | `bmad-testarch-automate` | expanded tests with evidence |
14: | "Audit the tests" | `bmad-testarch-test-review` | test quality findings |
15: | "Create CI" | `bmad-testarch-ci` | CI configuration and verified runs |
16: | "Set up test framework" | `bmad-testarch-framework` | framework, running examples |
17: | "Nonfunctional readiness" | `bmad-testarch-nfr` | security/performance/reliability evidence assessment |
18: | "Trace criteria to tests" | `bmad-testarch-trace` | coverage/gate verdict |
19: | "Review requirements/docs" | `bmad-review` or installed editorial/PM workflow | document review findings |
20: | "Ready to release R1?" | evidence collection + relevant native TEA/Build checks | PASS / CONCERNS / FAIL / UNVERIFIED, with blockers |
21: 
22: For a vague `qa feature`: inspect code, test inventory and acceptance criteria;
23: choose next meaningful QA work (often run existing tests first). If very
24: materially ambiguous (e.g., "QA" could mean review-only vs write-test-suites
25: with hours of work) ask one scope question; do not always ask by default.
26: 
27: For a ticket-to-PR lane, Build's native review is enough for a low-risk change
28: unless gaps exist; don't stack a redundant independent review by ritual. Use
29: risk-based extra TEA coverage on authentication, payment, data integrity,
30: authorization, migrations, privacy and critical reliability changes.
31: 
32: ## Release evaluation != release deployment
33: 
34: - Determine exact tag/commit, branch, environment, migration and rollback
35:   plan. Fetch real check outputs, failures, warnings and known waivers.
36: - Test checklist: required lint, typechecks, unit/integration/e2e, build,
37:   smoke, dependency/auth checks and CI per repo policy; NFR/trace when needed.
38: - Distinguish `PASS`, `FAIL`, `NOT RUN`, `NOT AVAILABLE`, `PENDING`; never infer
39:   PASS because no failure was mentioned.
40: - Status report must name exact covered commit SHA and environment. A QA gate
41:   cannot approve an untested changed SHA just because tests passed previously.
42: - Result: `ready` only with required evidence; `not ready` with concrete
43:   blockers; `unverified` with missing evidence. Explicit waivers are traceable.
44: - "Get ready for release" permits ordinary reversible corrections; not
45:   pushing to production, deleting resources or overriding branch protections.

2: 
3: ## Planning vs implementation
4: 
5: - "Create epics/stories" -> planning owner (v6 epic/story writer, v7 PO /

7:   acceptance, dependencies, risks, and estimates only when grounded.
8: - "Refine 1.1" -> native ticket/story refinement in owning runtime; preserve
9:   ID, owner, scope and accepted decisions. Don't implement until asked.
10: - "Implement 1.1" -> single-ticket lane in ticket-to-pr.md.
11: - "Finish epic 2" -> verify epic's native done conditions, run ready stories
12:   respecting dependencies, integration checks, trace, retrospective; output
13:   one PR per story by default unless user/repo policy says one epic PR.
14: - "Finish sprint" -> explicit bounded scope and authorization; use an
15:   installed actual orchestrator if available, don't write your own loop.
16: 
17: ## v6 and v7 state owners
18: 
19: v6: locate the correct `sprint-status.yaml`, story artifacts, approved epics and
20: readiness state. Don't guess status values: consult installed sprint-planning/
21: Build definitions. Do not mark done based solely on a worker claiming success.
22: 
23: v7 preview: locate initiative, epic and `tickets.toml` plan (or spec-derived
24: story registry if applicable), inspect `tickets.py` help and exact native
25: commands. `tickets.py next` may identify ready work; use only the installed
26: script's documented arguments. Preserve dependencies (`after`), stable IDs and
27: plan state. Don't directly rewrite structured TOML if native writer exists.
28: 
29: ## Selecting multi-ticket engine
30: 
31: 1. Existing project configured with official `bmad-loop`? Inspect `bmad-loop`
32:    CLI and project config, confirm version compatibility and select the native
33:    `--story`/`--epic`/bounded run interface if installed. Never claim it can
34:    dispatch a ticket tree source not supported in **that** installed version.
35: 2. Explicitly configured `auto-bmad` or `BAD`? Check its supported BMAD
36:    version, host, state format, and runner; ask before using archived or stale
37:    compatibility contracts. Do not force a deprecated 7-step legacy pipeline.
38: 3. No engine? In an interactive host, one coordinator session may dispatch
39:    native Build for ready work sequentially, read result and repeat while
40:    session limits permit; every Build owns one unit. No background promise.
41: 4. Parallel execution only when dependency-independent, git-isolated worktrees,
42:    bounded concurrency, distinct ownership and collision/conflict policy exist.
43:    Default is sequential (max 1), even for broad sprints.
44: 
45: ## Completion and proof
46: 
47: A complete epic needs all required stories verified, integration and regression
48: checks on the aggregated change, explicit deferred-work decision, QA gates
49: where appropriate, and native retrospective/acceptance. One passing story does
50: not mean epic PASS. No merge/deploy without separate authorization.

2: 
3: This is a DELIVERY CONTRACT, not an implementation workflow. The installed

8:

10: 
11: 1. Resolve task ID in the **current actual** backlog. v6: story source / sprint
12:    status / implementation artifacts. v7 preview: ticket registry, `tickets.py`
13:    and plan state. Do not assume `1.1` == `1-1` == GitHub issue #11 until proven.
14:    When exactly one matching ticket exists, show title and acceptance target.
15: 2. Read existing requirements, linked ADRs, dependencies, ticket status, related
16:    specs, previous build commits, and relevant tests. If already done, examine
17:    current branch/PR: report or continue missing delivery, don't rebuild.
18: 3. Preflight `git status`, current branch/base, remote, auth and existing PR.
19:    Dirty tree: preserve it, isolate safely in an approved clean worktree or ask.
20:    Never stash/reset/drop someone else's edits unilaterally. Prefer a
21:    `bmad/<ticket>-<slug>` topic branch or project naming policy.
22: 4. Check readiness. Block on unfinished hard dependencies, ambiguous scope,
23:    incompatible architecture, high-risk unresolved product choices. Ask a

26:    - `--local` / `--no-pr`: stay local.
